quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Rest your hand on the clutch and brake.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Drive below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rest your hand on the clutch and brake.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, rest your hand on the clutch and brake. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required for effective eye or face shield protection?

options.text: It must fasten securely.
It must be too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses.
It must be free of scratches.
It must allow clear side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be scratch-free, fasten securely, allow clear side vision, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed. It should allow air to pass through to prevent fogging.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. When is this part NOT safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: It is never safe for motorcyclists.
When the road is wet.
When it is sunny outside.
It is always safe.

questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. This strip is usually safe for motorcyclists unless the road is wet. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride to one side and stay in the center lane.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride your motorcycle between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, if traffic is heavy.
Yes, to prevent traffic jams during the day.
Yes, if the rider is comfortable.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, it is illegal for motorcycles and mopeds to pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help increase a rider's visibility?

options.text: Wearing proper clothing
Using your headlight at all times
Using your turn signals
Waving at other drivers

questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light. Waving does not improve visibility.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which is NOT important?

options.text: It must meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
It must fit snugly.
It must have no defects.
It must be attractive.

questions.explanation: A helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fit snugly all around, and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance does not matter.

questions.question: Which action is NOT safe for preventing fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting your distance to one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from the elements. Avoid artificial stimulants, as they can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing sound from the rear.
The back end jerks from side to side.
You cannot accelerate.
The rear brake stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a rear tire fails, the back of the motorcycle jerks from side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least one hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may come back into your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side of the lane nearest the passing vehicle is safer.
You will feel a stronger wind blast on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may come back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay on the side of your lane closest to the passing vehicle. If you move to the far side, the passing driver may think it is safe to return to your lane before it actually is.

questions.question: Which is NOT required for an eye or face shield to work well?

options.text: Free of scratches.
Resistant to penetration.
Fastens securely.
Airtight.

questions.explanation: A good eye shield or face shield must be free of scratches, resistant to penetration, give clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: Where should you ride to be seen in the rearview mirror of the driver ahead of you?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left side of your lane.
In the right side of your lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind another vehicle. This puts you directly in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Speed up.
Do not worry and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster and increase danger. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect to see you there.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.
Ride faster than usual.
Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances. Slow down and increase your following distance. Use your high beam whenever you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars?

options.text: Much less distance.
Less distance.
The same distance.
More distance.

questions.explanation: In traffic, a motorcycle needs as much stopping distance as a car does.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they feel comfortable.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch over them from the back.

questions.question: What can help reduce your chances of an accident?

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Focus only on your controls and not the road ahead.
Let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Why should you check your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: Only a mechanic can do a useful check.
You should not check before a ride.
You should only check after a ride.
It can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or broken equipment that could put you in danger.

questions.question: What is an important feature of a face shield?

options.text: It should give a clear view to both sides.
It should block all air flow.
It should be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting under it.
It should not fasten too tightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should give a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, resistant to penetration, provide clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When riding conditions are normal.
When the roadway is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
Weave between the three portions of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Staying close to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Staying too far away may encourage the other driver to merge back too soon.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of a proper lane position?

options.text: It increases your ability to see and be seen.
It helps you avoid surface hazards.
It helps you avoid traffic signals.
It communicates your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind gusts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also prevents other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape danger.

questions.question: Where are motorcycles most likely to have conflicts with other traffic?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other traffic. Stay alert at intersections where other vehicles may cross your path.

questions.question: What should you do to make a quick stop on wet pavement?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on wet pavement. Apply the front brake gradually to avoid locking it on a slippery surface.
